title: Insights from Optimizing HPL Performance on Exascale Systems: A Comparative Analysis of Panel Factorization
problem: HPL performance on exascale systems is sensitive to many interacting parameters; optimizing panel factorization for heterogeneous GPU-CPU systems is non-trivial
motivation: Exascale systems like Frontier are architecturally complex; HPL is primary benchmark for evaluating supercomputing performance; parameter tuning guidance is essential
method: The researchers tested HPL (a benchmark that measures supercomputer performance using large matrix operations) on Frontier, a supercomputer combining GPUs and CPUs. They built performance models to understand different strategies for panel factorization, which decomposes matrices by breaking them into manageable sections. They developed two approaches: one using dedicated CPU threads to manage work, and another running the factorization directly on GPU hardware using HIP cooperative groups (parallel programming tools that let GPU threads coordinate and share work).
key_novelty: Running panel factorization (the matrix decomposition step) directly on GPUs using HIP cooperative groups outperforms running it on CPUs on Frontier.
contributions: First HPL analysis on Frontier achieving 1.35 exaflops
Two novel PDFACT strategies (DT and GPUPDFACT)
Best practices and key performance factors for exascale HPL optimization

metrics.efficiency: Speedup of GPUPDFACT vs CPU PDFACT

limitations: Insights may be specific to Frontier architecture; generalization to other exascale systems not fully explored
primary_theme: Exascale system optimization via advanced factorization strategies
